Python 以縮排界定區塊。<code>if</code>、<code>for: Python uses indentation to delimit blocks. The headers of statements such as if, for, def, and class end with a colon, and their bodies are indented one level further. Engineering projects typically use four spaces per level. Four spaces is a style convention; the actual syntax requirement is consistent block indentation. Do not mix tabs and spaces. Lines can break naturally inside parentheses, which is usually easier to maintain than trailing backslashes.
名稱區分大小寫；<code>pump_id</code> 與 <code>Pum: Names are case-sensitive: pump_id and Pump_ID are different names. Names cannot begin with a digit. Python allows certain Unicode characters in identifiers, but mixing look-alike characters makes review more difficult. Use consistent naming conventions for equipment identifiers and function names. # begins an inline comment. The first string in a function, class, or module can serve as a docstring, accessible to help() and other tools. A triple-quoted string is not, in itself, general comment syntax.
<code>class</code>、<code>return</code>、<: Reserved words such as class, return, and None cannot be used as ordinary variable names. A soft keyword has syntactic meaning only in specific contexts, as in the relevant uses of match, case, _, and type. Query the current interpreter directly for the complete list to avoid mixing lists from different versions. Built-in names such as list and str are not reserved words, but you should avoid shadowing them with variables of the same name.
